## Trial `transit-traffic-acl-ubuntu24__P4EYyKq`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes of the task — TCP/8080 connectivity, TCP/23 rejection, and untouched pass-through of other traffic (ICMP) between node2 and node3 via node1 — are directly and repeatedly demonstrated, both before and after a full restart of all three nodes. The independent node-restart evidence protocol is well satisfied: pre/post boot identities differ and are corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and functional recovery (addressing, routing, forwarding sysctls, ACL, SONiC container stack, and end-to-end 8080/23/ICMP behavior) is shown after each restart. The one hygiene concern is an unrelated, persisted mutation to node1's pre-existing docker0 configuration that was not required by the task contract.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.880 | 46/3 (+8 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **tcp-8080-passthrough — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 can reach each other on TCP port 8080 through node1
  - **Why:** Bidirectional TCP/8080 connections succeeded with payload delivery (node2->node3 and node3->node2) both before and after node1's restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d2b21eb35b844430`, `cmd-c6bea9a3ed244487`, `cmd-771879cd0d484d4c`, `cmd-c0acf66fc2f446b2`, `cmd-dab8c27c665a4a71`, `cmd-106d20247bad49b2`
- **tcp-23-refused — Satisfied:** node1 refuses TCP port 23 passing between node2 and node3
  - **Why:** nft forward-chain rule rejects tcp dport 23 with a TCP reset; connection attempts fail in ~2ms (consistent with RST, not a timeout) in both directions, confirmed again after node1's restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f876663a989f4d16`, `cmd-d2b21eb35b844430`, `cmd-f3e33fa555644d02`, `cmd-771879cd0d484d4c`, `cmd-dab8c27c665a4a71`
- **other-traffic-untouched — Satisfied:** Rest of the forwarded traffic between node2 and node3 is left untouched
  - **Why:** ICMP (ping) between node2 and node3 across node1 succeeds with 0% loss, and the nft forward chain uses a default-accept policy with only the tcp/23 rule added, before and after restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d2b21eb35b844430`, `cmd-dab8c27c665a4a71`, `cmd-f876663a989f4d16`
- **restart-evidence-protocol — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes with pre-restart boot identity, acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/connectivity state
  - **Why:** All three nodes show a captured pre-restart boot_id, a reboot acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot_id (confirmed independently in the fixed after_executor snapshot: node1 db14b11b..., node2 e8fd5ab2..., node3 c723af0a...), and recovered state: node2/node3 addressing, routing, and ICMP recovered; node1's forwarding sysctls, ACL rule, interface addressing, and SONiC container stack recovered; full end-to-end functional re-verification (ICMP, TCP/8080, TCP/23-reject) succeeded through the restarted node1.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ed6febe9ea884440`, `cmd-3e0dcbc999f6422f`, `cmd-1d4b00b1e4f2485f`, `cmd-4df964f63c0c4218`, `cmd-12d6bf3a998e4638`, `cmd-a64b360472be4200`, `cmd-fae1a05738904f3b`, `cmd-ca29beba227940be`, `cmd-703ca2c4be4242b3`, `cmd-18425f5a61044487`, `cmd-765c23c1d57a45bd`, `cmd-60b8f9ea0a9440f2`, `cmd-dab8c27c665a4a71`, `cmd-106d20247bad49b2`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. Most state-changing commands are directly tied to the task (interface addressing, forwarding sysctls, nftables ACL, persistence files/units, restart protocol) and were retained as intended, necessary residue. One mutation is scope creep: on node1 the executor deleted docker0's pre-existing class-E address (240.127.1.1/24, present in the before_prepare baseline) and additionally baked this removal into the persistent boot-time oneshot service, so it recurs on every future boot. This is unrelated to routing traffic between node2/node3 on the seg-a/seg-b networks and has no stated causal link to satisfying the ACL/forwarding requirement; it is a retained, non-reverted mutation of pre-existing (non-executor-created) state (cmd-a7740811076c4958, cmd-639e6ece46464da3). It is low-risk (docker0 was already down/no-carrier) but not justified by the task contract. A transient 'ip addr flush'/'dev duplicate' error in cmd-a7740811076c4958 was immediately corrected in cmd-c020ffed2d7640d8 with no lasting effect. Stopping node1's interfaces-config.service reconciler was a necessary prerequisite to keep the static eth1/eth2 addressing from being reverted, so not penalized.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-a7740811076c4958`, `cmd-639e6ece46464da3`, `cmd-c020ffed2d7640d8`, `global:before_prepare:node1:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- ICMP was the only 'other traffic' type tested; no other protocols/ports were sampled to confirm the pass-through default-accept policy more broadly, though the nft ruleset configuration supports this by design.
- Post-restart end-to-end re-verification of TCP/23 rejection and ICMP was only explicitly re-run in the node2->node3 direction; the reverse direction was not re-tested after node1's restart (though the ACL/forwarding config recovery evidence for node1 applies symmetrically).
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.750); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.880; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
